title: Pastor, Thou Art from Us Taken
description: Pastor, Thou Art from Us Taken in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 598 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Pas-tor, thou art from us ta-ken In the glo-ry of thy years, As the oak, by tem-pests shak-en, Falls ere time its ver-dure sears.

lines: Pastor, thou art from us taken
In the glory of thy years,
As the oak, by tempests shaken,
Falls ere time its verdure sears.
Pale and cold we see thee lying
In God's temple, once so dear,
All thy love and zeal, to lead us
And on living bread to feed us,
May the conquering faith, that cheered thee
When thy foot on Jordan pressed,
Guide our spirits while we leave thee
In the tomb that Jesus blessed.

licence: Public domain: Lydia Sigourney died in 1865.
credits: Words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
